A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same two-stage bimodal LVLM jailbreak project, renamed from BAMBA to PBI-Attack. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original jailbreak benchmarks, transfer experiments, toxicity analyses, parameter studies and human evaluation involving 20 labelers.

after.justification: v3 reports original AdvBench and HADES evaluations, component ablations, transfer experiments, defense tests, timing measurements and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: v1 Section 4.2 uses GCG single-token substitutions and gradient-descent image updates. v3 replaces these with response-scored greedy selection of corpus suffixes and randomly generated image perturbations, followed by concatenation and superposition. Its prior-generation stage also explicitly optimizes a randomly initialized perturbation prefix. These revise the procedure beyond renaming the retained two-stage design.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on HADES text instructions representing five harmful scenarios (Appendix C), plus attacks against models using a random-image-perturbation defense (Section 6). AdvBench and the harmful initialization corpus remain. The separate human-rating calibration study and its participant population are removed.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Table 2, v3 Table 1 adds FigStep and HADES and removes CoJ and MRJ-Agent. InPieces comparisons against closed-source models become dashes. The corresponding attribute-wise toxicity plots also add GCG, which was absent from v1 Figures 5–6. These are changes within matched comparisons, beyond extending benchmarks.

E3.justification: AdvBench evaluation expands from 250 to 520 prompts. ASR changes from a summed-toxicity threshold of 1.5 calibrated by human ratings to HarmBench assessment with GPT-3.5-turbo. Main open-model experiments switch from MiniGPT-4 as the common surrogate to each target serving as its own surrogate. Transfer tables change from toxicity ratios to ASR. The reported OpenAI target changes from GPT-4o to GPT-4, without precise endpoint identifiers.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls comparing toxicity versus jailbreak-probability objectives and prior versus random initialization (Tables 2–3), perturbation-bound, candidate-count and interaction-step studies (Appendix B), efficiency comparisons and defense tests. The ten-query analysis is retained and relocated; the lambda study is updated. Human-threshold calibration and image-attention analysis disappear, while text-attention analysis and qualitative cases are revised and expanded.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated three times with means and standard deviations reported, and both average toxicity over ten responses per input pair. Neither introduces seed lists, confidence intervals or significance tests. Additional result rows and uncertainty bands follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main results are extensively replaced: MiniGPT-4 ASR is 98.4 ± 1.6 in v1 Table 2 and 94.9 ± 2.5 in v3 Table 1 under changed methods and evaluation settings. On Gemini, v1 ranks Arondight at 88.2 above BAMBA at 84.7; v3 ranks PBI-Attack at 71.7 above all comparators, including HADES at 63.5. Transfer results, toxicity profiles and lambda curves change, and HADES, component, timing and defense outcomes are added. These do not establish same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v3 introduces an explicit mathematical definition of image-perturbation superposition and an infinity-norm constraint on perturbation features, whereas v1 uses a generic image constraint space. Its feature-space update also invokes an inverse feature mapping. These are limited changes to the mathematical formulation; neither version provides theorems, proofs or convergence guarantees.

C1.justification: The claimed contribution of a new automatically evaluated, human-validated jailbreak criterion is removed. v3 redefines the technical contribution around greedy bidirectional black-box optimization and explicitly foregrounds surrogate-derived priors. Its abstract adds average ASR claims of 92.5% for white-box and 67.3% for black-box models. The underlying prior-plus-interaction concept and broad effectiveness claim remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive arguments that toxicity feedback can replace jailbreak-probability access, prior initialization improves attack effectiveness, and additional interaction strengthens harmful-feature injection. It also interprets the runtime–ASR tradeoff as worthwhile and explains random perturbations as disrupting attacks. The earlier human-threshold justification is removed. The limitation concerning slow model responses and expensive iterative attacks remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly reports a preferred image-candidate count of K=50, method-specific training and attack times, and the GPT-3.5-turbo judging dependency. The detailed human-labeling protocol disappears, and the numerical toxicity stopping threshold specified in v1 is no longer supplied. Hardware and most implementation hyperparameters remain unchanged; neither PDF adds project code-access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting FigStep, HADES, HarmBench and additional red-teaming and survey context. It recharacterizes UMK's limitation from single-round operation to one-way cross-modal interaction. Most earlier literature remains, including CoJ and MRJ-Agent despite their removal from experiments. The two HADES bibliography entries represent the same work, not distinct additions.

P1.justification: Beyond the title and method rename, v3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction and methodology. It integrates the separate multi-round related-work subsection, moves ablations into Appendix B, replaces the main-text case-study section with Appendix D examples, and introduces a defense section. These substantially alter the narrative and document organization.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the opening multi-round cartoon with an attack-comparison diagram and redraws the pipeline. It revises the text-attention display, removes the image-attention and human-voting figures, expands transfer tables to six targets, and adds component, timing, defense and HADES tables. Ablation plots are regrouped in Appendix B, and the toxicity plots gain another comparator. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited validation of its central components: Tables 2–3 isolate the objective and prior, Appendix B tests interaction and perturbations, and timing and defense experiments expose practical constraints. The explicit greedy second-stage procedure and separation of ASR judging from the optimized toxicity score also strengthen the paper. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including removal of human validation and the numerical stopping threshold, incorrect gain annotations in Table 5, and reversed white-box/black-box averages in the conclusion. The improvement concerns methodological support and evaluation quality, not higher cross-version scores.
